problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: The inclusion combines the Lipschitz operator F with a set-valued monotone operator A accessible through its resolvent.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: F(x)=n⁻¹∑ᵢFᵢ(x), with n>0; the component operators need not be gradients.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Find a zero of F+A, where F is single-valued and A is monotone. A solution x⋆ satisfies ⟨F(y)+v,y−x⋆⟩≥−ρ‖F(y)+v‖² for every v∈A(y), with 0≤ρL<1. Monotonicity of F is not required.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Exact resolvent evaluations Jη(z) satisfying (z−Jη(z))/η∈A(Jη(z)) for every η>0. Component and resolvent queries each consume one call from the same fixed budget.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumWeakMintyInclusion.lean: spec.Query and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm.query and executeWithTrace.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact indexed component evaluations Fᵢ(x), independent of history and oracle seed. No gradient structure or stochastic oracle error is assumed.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumWeakMintyInclusion.lean: spec.Query and first oracle equality in spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Real Hilbert space, potentially infinite-dimensional. The average operator is L-Lipschitz and n⁻¹∑ᵢ‖Fᵢ(x)−Fᵢ(y)‖²≤Λ²‖x−y‖², with 0<L≤Λ. A weak-Minty solution lies within distance R of x0. All parameters, including n,L,Λ,ρ,R,ε,x0 and the ambient space, are public; the component operators, A, and solution are hidden. No bounded component variance or bounded domain is assumed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumWeakMintyInclusion.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.valid, and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The squared-residual guarantee is in expectation under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The returned certificate satisfies v∈A(x) almost surely; residual accuracy itself is only required in expectation.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: Return a measurable pair (x,v) whose squared inclusion residual is integrable and satisfies E‖F(x)+v‖²≤ε². This is an inclusion residual, not necessarily a gradient norm.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: A structured nonmonotone inclusion with a weak-Minty solution, separate average and mean-square component Lipschitz constants, and an explicit residual certificate in a general Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
Finite-Sum Weak Minty Inclusions

We consider finding x∈E with 0∈F(x)+T(x) in a real Hilbert space E, where F=n−1∑i=1nFi averages n≥1 component maps Fi:E→E and T:E⇉E is monotone. The average is Lipschitz, component differences satisfy a mean-square Lipschitz bound, and a weak Minty solution lies within a prescribed distance of the given starting point. The oracle returns exact component values and resolvent evaluations of T. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable pair (x¯,v¯)∈E×E with v¯∈T(x¯) almost surely and EP∥F(x¯)+v¯∥2≤ε2, where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

More precisely, the inclusion is find x∈E such that 0∈F(x)+T(x),F(x)=1n∑i=1nFi(x). Write ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ for the inner product on E and ∥⋅∥ for its induced norm. The parameters satisfy n∈N,n≥1,0<L≤Λ,ρ≥0,ρL<1,R≥0,ε>0. The algorithm receives E,n,L,Λ,ρ,R,ε and the starting point x0∈E; the maps Fi and T are accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Monotonicity and resolvent access). For every x,y∈E, a∈T(x), and b∈T(y), ⟨a−b,x−y⟩≥0. There is a map J:R×E→E, written Jη(z), such that z−Jη(z)η∈T(Jη(z)),η>0,z∈E.

Assumption 2 (Finite-sum Lipschitz bounds). For all x,y∈E, ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,1n∑i=1n∥Fi(x)−Fi(y)∥2≤Λ2∥x−y∥2.

Assumption 3 (Weak Minty solution and initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that −F(x⋆)∈T(x⋆),∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, and, for every y∈E and v∈T(y), ⟨F(y)+v,y−x⋆⟩≥−ρ∥F(y)+v∥2.

A component query (i,x) returns Fi(x) for any i∈{1,…,n} and x∈E. A resolvent query (η,z) returns Jη(z) for any η∈R and z∈E; the stated resolvent condition applies when η>0. Each query of either kind counts as one call toward a common oracle-call budget.

After the allotted calls, the output (x¯,v¯) must be measurable, its squared residual must be integrable under P, and it must satisfy v¯∈T(x¯)P-a.s.,EP[∥F(x¯)+v¯∥2]≤ε2.

comparisonHtml:
In a real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure, F=n−1∑i=1nFi is L-Lipschitz and n−1∑i∥Fi(x)−Fi(y)∥2≤Λ2∥x−y∥2. The operator A is monotone with exact, everywhere-defined resolvents for every positive step size. There is x⋆ with 0∈F(x⋆)+A(x⋆), ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, and ⟨F(y)+v,y−x⋆⟩≥−ρ∥F(y)+v∥2 for every v∈A(y). Here n≥1, 0<L≤Λ, ρ,R≥0, ρL<1, and ε>0. The target is a measurable pair (Y,V) with V∈A(Y) almost surely and integrable squared residual satisfying ∫∥F(Y)+V∥2dP≤ε2, where P is the execution law. Each component evaluation or resolvent evaluation costs one call.

For τ=n/Λ, ρ<τ/2, and ρτL2≤c<1 fixed; target ∫∥Pτ(u)∥2dP≤τ2ε2.

 (1): Scope: graph weak Minty, arbitrary monotone A, and full ρL<1 range instead of (4)’s pairwise condition and restricted range. (1): ε−2 instead of ε−1 up to a logarithm. Different residual targets; no identical-output cost comparison established.

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic
import LongTails.Template

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace BigOperators
open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumWeakMintyInclusion

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  n : ℕ
  L : ℝ
  Λ : ℝ
  ρ : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE
  Params.measurableE Params.borelE

noncomputable def operator {E : Type*} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]
    {n : ℕ} (F : Fin n → E → E) (x : E) : E :=
  (n : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ i, F i x

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := (Fin p.n → p.E → p.E) × (p.E → Set p.E)
  Query p := (Fin p.n × p.E) ⊕ (ℝ × p.E)
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E × p.E
  publicInput := fun p => p
  valid p := 0 < p.n ∧ 0 < p.L ∧ p.L ≤ p.Λ ∧ 0 ≤ p.ρ ∧
    p.ρ * p.L < 1 ∧ 0 ≤ p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p I oracle :=
    ∃ J : ℝ → p.E → p.E,
      (∀ history seed i x, oracle.answer history (0, Sum.inl (i, x)) seed = I.1 i x) ∧
      (∀ history seed η z, oracle.answer history (0, Sum.inr (η, z)) seed = J η z) ∧
      (∀ η z, 0 < η → η⁻¹ • (z - J η z) ∈ I.2 (J η z)) ∧
      (∀ x y, ∀ a ∈ I.2 x, ∀ b ∈ I.2 y, 0 ≤ ⟪a - b, x - y⟫) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖operator I.1 x - operator I.1 y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x y, (p.n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, ‖I.1 i x - I.1 i y‖ ^ 2 ≤
        p.Λ ^ 2 * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2) ∧
      (∃ xstar, -operator I.1 xstar ∈ I.2 xstar ∧ ‖p.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ p.R ∧
        ∀ y, ∀ v ∈ I.2 y, -p.ρ * ‖operator I.1 y + v‖ ^ 2 ≤
          ⟪operator I.1 y + v, y - xstar⟫)
  successful p I output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), (output ω).2 ∈ I.2 (output ω).1) ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖operator I.1 (output ω).1 + (output ω).2‖ ^ 2) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, ‖operator I.1 (output ω).1 + (output ω).2‖ ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε ^ 2

end LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumWeakMintyInclusion
